Here is the Python code to classify the lines of the laboratory report:

```python
known_tests = {
    "718-7": "Haemoglobin",
    "789-8": "Red blood cells",
    "4544-3": "Haematocrit",
    "787-2": "MCV",
    "6690-2": "White blood cells",
    "777-3": "Platelets",
    "2498-4": "Iron",
    "2276-4": "Ferritin",
    "2345-7": "Glucose",
    "4548-4": "HbA1c",
    "2093-3": "Total cholesterol",
    "2085-9": "HDL cholesterol",
    "13457-7": "LDL cholesterol",
    "2571-8": "Triglycerides",
    "2160-0": "Creatinine",
    "3084-1": "Uric acid",
    "2951-2": "Sodium",
    "2823-3": "Potassium",
    "17861-6": "Calcium",
    "1742-6": "ALT",
    "1920-8": "AST",
    "2324-2": "GGT",
    "6768-6": "Alkaline phosphatase",
    "1975-2": "Total bilirubin",
    "1751-7": "Albumin",
    "3016-3": "TSH",
    "3024-7": "Free T4",
    "1988-5": "CRP",
    "62292-8": "Vitamin D (25-OH)",
    "2132-9": "Vitamin B12"
}

def classify_line(line):
    parts = line.split(":")
    number = parts[0].strip()
    test_name = parts[1].strip()
    if test_name in known_tests:
        return f"{number}|{known_tests[test_name]}"
    else:
        return f"{number}|NONE"

lines = [
    "1: Patient: Jonas Schmidt    Geburtsdatum: 10/12/1996",
    "2: HÄMOGLOBIN                  12.2 g/dl     (12.0 – 16.0)",
    "3: RBC                          5.2 10^6/ul  (4.0 - 5.5)",
    "4: HÄMATOKRIT                  47.2 %        (36.0 - 48.0)",
    "5: MCV                         68.3 fL       (80.0 – 100.0)",
    "6: LCUKOZYTEN (WBC)             2.9 10^3/uL  (4.0 – 10.0)",
    "7: THROMBOZYTEN               158.7 10^3/µl  (150.0-450.0)",
    "8: EISEN                       62.2 µg/dl    (50.0 - 170.0)",
    "9: FERRITIN                     9.1 ng/mL    (15.0 – 150.0)",
    "10: GLUKOSE                     84.6 mg/dL    (70.0-100.0)",
    "11: HBA1C                        7.4 %        (bis 5.7)",
    "12: CHOLES. GESAMT             191.6 mg/dL    (bis 200.0)",
    "13: HDL-CH0LESTERIN             66.3 mg/dL    (> 40.0)",
    "14: LDL-CHOLESTERIN             75.6 mg/dL    (bis 130.0)",
    "15: TRIGLYCERIDE               173.4 mg/dL    (< 150.0)",
    "16: KREATLNIN                    1.4 mg/dL    (0.5 - 1.1)",
    "17: HARNSÄURE                    3.6 mg/dL    (3.0 - 7.0)",
    "18: NATRIUM                    141.3 mmol/l   (136.0 – 145.0)",
    "19: KALIUM                       6.6 mmol/l   (3.5 – 5.1)",
    "20: CALCIUM (CA)                 7.7 mg/dL    (8.5-10.5)",
    "21: ALT (GPT)                   45.6 U/L      (bis 40.0)",
    "22: AST (GOT)                   45.6 U/L      (bis 40.0)",
    "23: GAMMA-GT (GGT)              43.1 u/l      (<50.0)",
    "24: ALKALISCHE PHOSPHATASE     104.2 U/L      (40.0 - 130.0)",
    "25: BILIRUBIN GESAMT             1.0 mg/dL    (0.3-1.2)",
    "26: A1BUMIN                      4.0 g/dL     (3.5 - 5.0)",
    "27: TSH                          0.3 mIU/L    (0.4-4.0)",
    "28: FT4                          0.9 ng/dL    (0.9 – 1.7)",
    "29: CRP                          6.7 mg/l     (<5.0)",
    "30: VITAMIN D (25-OH)           82.0 ng/ml    (30.0-100.0)",
    "31: VITAMI. B12                816.1 pg/ml    (200.0-900.0)",
    "32: Pag. 1/1"
]

for line in lines:
    print(classify_line(line))
```

This code defines a dictionary `known_tests` that maps LOINC codes to their corresponding English names. The `classify_line` function takes a line from the report as input, splits it into parts, and checks if the test name is in the `known_tests` dictionary. If it is, the function returns a line with the number and the corresponding LOINC code. If not, the function returns a line with the number and "NONE". The code then iterates over the lines of the report, calls the `classify_line` function for each line, and prints the result.
